nodes.label: Infrastructure investment in digital platforms
nodes.slide_anchor_title: Infrastructure and Scale in Digital Platforms
nodes.description: Spending on the physical and digital infrastructure needed to support online platforms, such as servers, networks, and data centers.
nodes.why_it_matters: Understanding infrastructure investment helps explain the costs and challenges behind running large-scale digital services and why efficiency is so important.

nodes.label: Cloud and data center capacity
nodes.slide_anchor_title: Infrastructure and Scale in Digital Platforms
nodes.description: The total amount of computing power and storage available in cloud services and data centers.
nodes.why_it_matters: Cloud and data center capacity determines how much digital work can be done, affecting everything from AI training to website hosting.

nodes.label: Data center efficiency
nodes.slide_anchor_title: Infrastructure and Scale in Digital Platforms
nodes.description: How effectively a data center uses its resources, such as energy and hardware, to deliver services.
nodes.why_it_matters: Improving data center efficiency reduces costs and environmental impact, making digital platforms more sustainable and profitable.

nodes.label: Pricing strategy
nodes.description: The approach a company takes to set prices for its products or services.
nodes.why_it_matters: Pricing strategy directly affects revenue, competitiveness, and how customers perceive value.

nodes.label: Price before product
nodes.description: A method where the target price is set first, and then the product is designed to fit that price.
nodes.why_it_matters: This approach ensures products are affordable for customers and profitable for the company.

nodes.label: Tiered pricing
nodes.description: Offering different pricing levels for different types of customers or usage amounts.
nodes.why_it_matters: Tiered pricing helps companies serve a wider range of customers and maximize revenue.

nodes.label: Price differentiation
nodes.description: Adjusting prices for different customers or situations to maximize sales and profits.
nodes.why_it_matters: Price differentiation allows businesses to better match what customers are willing to pay, increasing overall value.

nodes.label: Enterprise pricing breakpoints
nodes.description: Specific points where enterprise pricing changes, often based on approval levels or purchase size.
nodes.why_it_matters: Recognizing pricing breakpoints helps companies structure deals that align with how large organizations make buying decisions.

nodes.label: Special pricing for customer segments
nodes.description: Discounts or special offers targeted at specific groups, like students or educators.
nodes.why_it_matters: Special pricing can attract new customers and build long-term loyalty from valuable segments.

nodes.label: Lifetime value of a customer
nodes.description: The total profit a company expects to earn from a customer over the entire relationship.
nodes.why_it_matters: Focusing on lifetime value helps businesses make smarter decisions about marketing, pricing, and customer retention.

nodes.label: Pricing complexity
nodes.description: The increasing difficulty of managing pricing as more exceptions, discounts, and special cases are added over time.
nodes.why_it_matters: Pricing complexity can make systems harder to manage and understand, leading to errors and inefficiencies.

nodes.label: Merchant systems
nodes.description: The systems and processes businesses use to handle sales, payments, and customer interactions.
nodes.why_it_matters: Merchant systems are essential for running online businesses smoothly and securely.

nodes.label: Legacy system integration
nodes.description: The challenge of connecting and updating older systems with new technologies.
nodes.why_it_matters: Legacy system integration is crucial for keeping businesses up-to-date without losing valuable data or functionality.

nodes.label: Batch processing in legacy systems
nodes.description: Older systems that process data in large groups at scheduled times, rather than instantly.
nodes.why_it_matters: Understanding batch processing helps explain why some legacy systems are slow or hard to update.

nodes.label: Documentation and maintenance challenges
nodes.description: Problems that arise when systems are poorly documented or hard to maintain over time.
nodes.why_it_matters: Good documentation and maintenance are key to keeping systems reliable and understandable as they age.

nodes.label: Payment infrastructure
nodes.description: The technology and processes that allow businesses to accept and manage electronic payments.
nodes.why_it_matters: Payment infrastructure is the backbone of online commerce, affecting security, speed, and customer trust.

nodes.label: Fraud and transaction risk
nodes.description: The risk of fraudulent transactions and financial losses in payment systems.
nodes.why_it_matters: Managing fraud and transaction risk is essential to protect both businesses and customers.

nodes.label: Chargebacks and retailer risk
nodes.description: The risk retailers face when customers dispute charges and payments are reversed.
nodes.why_it_matters: Chargebacks can lead to significant financial losses, so understanding and managing this risk is important for retailers.

nodes.label: Tax compliance in online payments
nodes.description: The need to correctly handle taxes, like VAT, when processing online payments.
nodes.why_it_matters: Tax compliance is critical to avoid legal issues and unexpected costs for online businesses.

nodes.label: Customer relationship management
nodes.description: Systems and strategies for managing interactions and relationships with customers.
nodes.why_it_matters: Effective customer relationship management can improve satisfaction, loyalty, and business success.

nodes.label: Customer service as competitive advantage
nodes.description: Using excellent customer service to stand out from competitors and attract more customers.
nodes.why_it_matters: Great customer service can help a business win loyal customers and gain a bigger share of the market.

nodes.label: Continuity of customer experience
nodes.description: Ensuring customers have a smooth and consistent experience across all touchpoints and support channels.
nodes.why_it_matters: Consistency in customer experience builds trust and keeps customers coming back, even when support is spread across different locations.

nodes.label: Personalisation
nodes.description: Tailoring products, services, or experiences to individual customer preferences and behaviors.
nodes.why_it_matters: Personalisation helps increase customer retention by making each interaction feel relevant and valuable.

nodes.label: Behavioral segmentation
nodes.description: Grouping customers based on their actions and behaviors rather than just demographics.
nodes.why_it_matters: Behavioral segmentation allows businesses to better understand and target customers based on what they actually do, leading to more effective marketing.

nodes.label: Socio-economic classification
nodes.description: Classifying people based on their social and economic status.
nodes.why_it_matters: Socio-economic classification is a traditional way to segment markets, but may not capture actual customer behavior online.

nodes.label: Customer personas
nodes.description: Fictional profiles that represent different types of customers a business wants to target.
nodes.why_it_matters: Customer personas help businesses visualize and plan for the needs and behaviors of their key customer groups.

nodes.label: High-expectation users
nodes.description: Users who have high standards and can influence others by sharing their experiences.
nodes.why_it_matters: Identifying high-expectation users helps businesses focus on the most influential customers who can drive growth.

nodes.label: Internationalisation challenges
nodes.description: Difficulties and complexities businesses face when expanding to international markets.
nodes.why_it_matters: Understanding these challenges is crucial for successfully operating in different countries and cultures.

nodes.label: Variation in languages and currencies
nodes.description: Differences in language and currency that affect how businesses operate in various countries.
nodes.why_it_matters: Adapting to local languages and currencies is essential for reaching and serving international customers effectively.

nodes.label: Legal and regulatory differences
nodes.description: Differences in laws and regulations between countries that affect business operations.
nodes.why_it_matters: Complying with local laws is necessary to avoid legal issues and operate smoothly in global markets.

nodes.label: Monetisation models
nodes.description: Different ways a business can earn revenue from its products or services.
nodes.why_it_matters: Choosing the right monetisation model is key to a business’s financial success.

nodes.label: Freemium model
nodes.description: A business model where basic services are free, but users pay for premium features.
nodes.why_it_matters: The freemium model can attract a large user base and convert some users into paying customers.

nodes.label: Subscription and pay-per-use models
nodes.description: Business models where customers pay a recurring fee (subscription) or pay each time they use a service (pay-per-use).
nodes.why_it_matters: These models provide predictable revenue and can suit different types of products or services.

nodes.label: Cost per acquisition and lifetime value
nodes.description: Metrics that track how much it costs to acquire a customer and how much value that customer brings over time.
nodes.why_it_matters: Understanding these numbers helps businesses make smart decisions about marketing and growth.

nodes.label: Brand awareness
nodes.description: How well customers recognize and remember a brand.
nodes.why_it_matters: Strong brand awareness builds trust and makes it easier to attract and retain customers.

nodes.label: Keyword advertising
nodes.description: Online advertising that targets users based on specific search terms or keywords.
nodes.why_it_matters: Keyword advertising helps businesses reach potential customers who are actively searching for related products.

nodes.label: Click-through metrics
nodes.description: Measurements of how often users click on ads or links.
nodes.why_it_matters: Click-through metrics show how effective online ads are at attracting attention and driving action.

nodes.label: Network effects
nodes.description: The phenomenon where a product or service becomes more valuable as more people use it.
nodes.why_it_matters: Network effects can help a business grow rapidly and become dominant in its market.

nodes.label: User-generated content
nodes.description: Content created and shared by users rather than the business itself.
nodes.why_it_matters: User-generated content can drive engagement and add value to online platforms.

nodes.label: Chicken-and-egg problem
nodes.description: The challenge of needing both users and content (or buyers and sellers) to make a platform valuable.
nodes.why_it_matters: Solving the chicken-and-egg problem is crucial for launching successful online platforms.

nodes.label: Disintermediation
nodes.description: Disintermediation is the process of removing intermediaries or middlemen from a supply chain, allowing producers to connect directly with consumers.
nodes.why_it_matters: Understanding disintermediation helps explain how businesses can reduce costs and potentially increase efficiency by cutting out unnecessary steps in the value chain.

nodes.label: Direct producer-to-consumer relationships
nodes.description: Direct producer-to-consumer relationships occur when producers sell their products or services straight to consumers, bypassing traditional intermediaries like wholesalers or retailers.
nodes.why_it_matters: This concept is important because it shows how businesses can gain more control over distribution and customer relationships, but also need to consider the value intermediaries previously provided.

nodes.label: Analytics and data-driven strategy
nodes.description: Analytics and data-driven strategy involve using data and analytical tools to guide business decisions and strategies.
nodes.why_it_matters: This is crucial because data-driven approaches can lead to better decision-making, but also require careful interpretation to avoid misleading conclusions.

nodes.label: Bias in data analytics
nodes.description: Bias in data analytics refers to the presence of systematic errors or prejudices in data analysis, often reflecting existing patterns or inequalities.
nodes.why_it_matters: Recognizing bias is essential for making fair and accurate decisions based on data, as unaddressed biases can reinforce existing problems.
